title: pi <= 4, from the same geometric domination the construction already needed
statement: le pi four, four := mul two two. Every partial sum of the series is at most two: termwise piHalfTerm k <= (1/2)^k (CReal.piHalfTermLePowHalf, a short induction on the definitional ratio (k+1)/(2k+3) <= 1/2), summed by CReal.sumRange_le, then CReal.sumRange_pow_half_closed_form reads the geometric partial sum as 2*(1 - (1/2)^n) <= 2. That holds at EVERY index including 0, so CReal.converges_upper_bound applies with no shift, giving CReal.piHalfLeTwo : le piHalf two; pi IS mul two piHalf, so one CReal.mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left finishes. Looser than the classical 3.15 for the same structural reason CReal.e_le_four is looser than e <= 3: sharpening needs the tail dominated from index 4 rather than from index 0, a re-indexed domination rather than a corollary of what is here.
